title: Variational Autoencoders
overview: A VAE learns a probabilistic latent space: the encoder outputs a distribution rather than a point. Sampling from the prior then lets the decoder generate new data.
objectives: Explain the ELBO with its reconstruction and KL terms
Generate samples from the latent prior

method.title: Probabilistic encoder
method.body: The encoder outputs a mean and log-variance defining a Gaussian q(z|x).

method.title: Reparameterization
method.body: Sample z = mu + sigma * eps with eps ~ N(0, I) so gradients flow through the sampling step.

method.title: ELBO
method.body: The loss combines reconstruction error with KL(q(z|x) || N(0, I)), which regularizes the latent space.

method.title: Generation
method.body: Draw z from N(0, I) and decode it to produce a new sample.

pseudocode:
mu, logvar = encoder(x)
eps = randn_like(mu)
z = mu + exp(0.5*logvar) * eps
recon = decoder(z)
kl = -0.5 * sum(1 + logvar - mu**2 - exp(logvar))
loss = recon_loss(recon, x) + kl

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
mu = np.array([0.5, -1.0]); logvar = np.array([0.0, -2.0])
kl = -0.5 * np.sum(1 + logvar - mu ** 2 - np.exp(logvar))
print("KL to N(0, I):", round(float(kl), 4))
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
eps = rng.normal(size=(5000, 2))
z = mu + np.exp(0.5 * logvar) * eps
print("sample mean:", np.round(z.mean(0), 2))
print("sample std: ", np.round(z.std(0), 2))
